comments.body: James Griffin, are you done with this ticket? If so, please add a link to your pull-request as a comment here.
Please see the following pull-request: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/841

Please note that I have pushed an additional 2 commits in relation to the pull-request (following a discussion in relation to the Exception class raised in response to the PUT operation), and that Travis CI now indicates that the build is passing: https://travis-ci.org/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/builds/72325274

When I test the exact example noted in this ticket, the resource is successfully created. Did you test this James Griffin?
See code review comments.

It appears that this comment still needs to be addressed:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/841/files#r36138821

Sorry for the back-and-forth on this ticket, James Griffin, but could you please rebase your PR on master... again?
Thanks.

Sorry for the back-and-forth on this ticket, James R. Griffin III, but could you please rebase your PR on master... again?

My apologies Andrew Woods, the fault lies with me (and I greatly appreciate your patience with these exchanges).

I believe that I have rebased the PR on the branch master successfully.

This is what I do:

  • Ensure my master branch is up to date:
    git checkout master
    git pull
  • Ensure my ".git/config" is set correctly, see: https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Guide+for+New+Developers#GuideforNewDevelopers-ConfigureforPerformingCodeReviews
  • Checkout your branch: pull/841
    git checkout --track origin pull/841
  • Rebase on master
    git rebase master
    ...see rebase conflicts.

Since your changes are fairly limited, I would suggest you just create a new branch from master, and reimplement your few updates, then submit a new PR. Your pull/841 branch simply has problems... not worth untangling.

Dear Andrew Woods,

In response to this, I have closed https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/841, and opened https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/901 using a branch from a new fork (cloned anew after these failed attempts to rebase from master).

I shall pursue the identification of solutions for these issues in order to avoid any the falling of any forked or local branches out of parity with the structure of the upstream code base.

Thank you again.

POST generates a resource at
http://localhost:8080/rest/3d/5b/53/28/3d5b5328-ab8e-4e19-8308-b458b897e8f2

PUT to

  • http://localhost:8080/rest/3d/test
  • http://localhost:8080/rest/3d/5b/test
  • http://localhost:8080/rest/3d/5b/53/test
  • http://localhost:8080/rest/3d/5b/53/28/test
    all fail with the correct response.

But a PUT to http://localhost:8080/rest/3d/5b/53/28/3d5b5328-ab8e-4e19-8308-b458b897e8f2/test succeeds.

Someone else should probably review the Java code though.

This is the same issue as described in:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1505

but instead of preventing POSTing to pairtree resources, this task is to prevent PUTting to pairtree resources.

For example, if a resource has been created with a POST /rest request such that it exists at the following URL:
http://localhost:8080/rest/76/9e/2f/b5/769e2fb5-fa2c-42cc-a467-3482b6a9a721

The following request should fail with a 403:
curl -i -XPUT localhost:8080/rest/76/9e/test
